kicker: THANKSGIVING NIGHT · MARKETS CLOSED THU · FRIDAY HALF DAY, STOCKS CLOSE 1:00PM
headline: S&P perps near 7,300. Chips keep pulling the bounce higher.
lede: S&P perps are up about 1.7% vs Wednesday's close and about 1% since 4pm, led by memory and chip names. Nasdaq 100 perps are up about 2.5%.
pills: NVDA export curbs · S&P credit watch
drivers: Since 4pm: SK Hynix perp +6.1%, MU +4.5%, AMD +4.3%, SMH +2.7%, NVDA +2.1%. In Tokyo, Kioxia and Socionext up 5% to 6%.
Kospi +2.2% to 4,813 and Nikkei +0.7% to 57,919 in Friday morning trade. Korea 200 perp +3.7% since 4pm.
Iran says mines hit ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent $96.29, WTI $85.43, up 2.1%. Keeps inflation and Fed hike fears alive.
Server shipments to four SE Asian countries halted under new curbs. S&P has its AA rating on watch for a cut. Huang hearings Dec 1 and Dec 3.
picks: S&P perps at 7,306, +1.7% vs Wed close and +1.0% since 4pm. Nasdaq 100 perps +2.5% vs Wed. SK Hynix +6.1%, MU +4.5%, AMD +4.3% since 4pm.
Tokyo chip and power names lead: Socionext +6%, Kioxia +5%, IHI and Resonac near +6%. SoftBank and Tokyo Electron down about 3%.
Friday morning in Asia: Nikkei +0.7% to 57,919, Kospi +2.2% to 4,813, Hang Seng +0.4%, ASX +0.4%. Shanghai −0.1%.
WTI +2.1% to $85.43 as it catches up after the holiday. Brent $96.29, −0.3%. Yen at 159.25 per dollar.
CME equity futures reopen after the 1:00pm holiday halt.
Brent settles $96.57, +1.2%, third straight gain and about 8% in 3 sessions. Saudi says air defenses intercepted drones aimed at Ras Tanura.
Iran says mines struck ships in the Strait of Hormuz, reviving supply fears.
FT: Nvidia tells Dell and Supermicro to stop server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under new US export curbs.
Asia rebounds: Nikkei +0.9%, SoftBank +7.3%, Kioxia +12.6% on an Nvidia memory demo, Taiex +2.5%. Kospi +0.3% after −6.2%.
Huang faces a closed door House interview Dec 1, then public Senate Banking testimony Dec 3.
Wed close: S&P 7,182.78 (−0.25%) after a 3.2% intraday drop. See the Wed recap tab.
means: Perps near 7,300 put the implied open about 100 points above 7,201, Wednesday's bull trigger. Chips leading is the confirmation that was missing.
A gap this size on a half day can fade. Holding above 7,201 after 9:30am keeps the bounce; back under it puts the 7,060 to 7,200 range back in play.
Oil is the risk. Brent near $96 with mines in Hormuz feeds inflation fears and a Dec 9 hike that is already priced at 97.8%.
Thin books. Moves can be exaggerated both ways, like Wednesday.
calendar: Europe opens 3:00am. Watch if Asia's chip bid carries
Advance goods trade, retail and wholesale inventories
Black Friday reads. Adobe forecast: $12.9B online, +9.2%
Huang before House Dec 1, Senate Banking Dec 3
impNote: Perps (the xyz market on Liquid) trade 24/7 and can run ahead of CME futures in thin holiday hours. CME ES and NQ reopened 6:00pm ET. Options levels are from Wednesday, the last session.
